name: ManagedApp
summary: Customize your app for managed deployments by providing configurable features that rely on secure access to secrets and data that an administrator provisions.

declarations.name: ManagedAppCertificatesProvider
declarations.comment:
A class that provides certificates that an MDM admin provisions for a managed app or extension.

Create an instance of this class when your app needs to access certificates that the MDM admin provisions for your app from their MDM server.

members.name: certificate
members.signature: func certificate(withIdentifier identifier: String) async throws(ManagedAppError) -> SecCertificate
members.comment:
Provides a certificate by its identifier.

The MDM server can update the certificate at any time. After that, ``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers`` yields a new array of identifiers. Call this method again to obtain the updated certificate.

The MDM server can change the available certificates at any time. When that happens, the list of valid identifiers updates accordingly. For example, the list of valid identifiers might change between the time that the app accesses
``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers`` and then calls this method passing in one of its elements. So, the app needs to handle the case that this method throws ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier``.

- Important: Avoid storing the certificate and instead, call this method whenever the app needs the certificate. For security reasons, avoid logging or displaying the certificate. Even though the certificate is a "public" certificate, it can contain sensitive information.

- Parameter identifier: The identifier of the requested certificate. This function throws ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier`` if the value you supply isn't currently in ``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers``.
- Returns: The requested certificate
- Throws: ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier`` if no certificate exists with the specified identifier.

members.name: identifiers
members.signature: var identifiers: some AsyncSequence<Array<String>, Never> { get async }
members.comment:
An asynchronous sequence of arrays of certificate identifiers provided by the MDM server.

Use ``ManagedAppCertificatesProvider/certificate(withIdentifier:)`` to look up an identifier
to obtain the associated certificate. The sequence yields an array of identifiers when:
* You begin iterating this property using `for await`.
* The list of certificate identifiers changes.
* The value of one or more certificates changes.

You define the values of the identifiers that an MDM admin can use. Define specific individual values or ranges of
values to group certificates, or use the configuration to determine the meaning of the identifiers.

This property yields an empty array if the MDM admin hasn't provisioned any certificates for your app.

members.name: init
members.comment: Initializes a managed app certificates provider.

declarations.name: ManagedAppConfigurationDecodingError
declarations.comment:
A protocol for an error that describes an issue with decoding the configuration.

For more information, see ``ManagedAppConfigurationProvider/configurations(_:)``.

declarations.name: ManagedAppConfigurationDecodingErrorCode
declarations.comment:
A code for an error that occurs during configuration decoding.

The system reserves some codes for its use only. Reserved codes are equal to or greater than `firstReserved`. Codes less than the `firstReserved` value are app-specific. For more information, see ``ManagedAppConfigurationDecodingError/code``.

members.name: keyNotFound
members.comment: An error code that indicates the decoder encountered an unknown coding key.

members.name: typeMismatch
members.comment: An error code that indicates the decoder encountered a type mismatch.

members.name: dataCorrupted
members.comment: An error code that indicates the decoder encountered corrupt data.

members.name: firstReserved
members.comment: An error code for the start of the range of reserved error codes.

members.name: valueNotFound
members.comment: An error code that indicates a coding key yields no value.

members.name: generic
members.comment: A reserved error that indicates the decoder threw an unknown custom error.

members.name: timeout
members.comment: An error code that indicates the decoder timed out.

members.name: init
members.comment: Initializes a configuration decoding error code.

members.name: rawValue
members.comment: The error code's value in its underlying type.

declarations.name: ManagedAppConfigurationDecodingErrorCode.RawValue
declarations.comment:
The raw type that can be used to represent all values of the conforming
type.

Every distinct value of the conforming type has a corresponding unique
value of the `RawValue` type, but there may be values of the `RawValue`
type that don't have a corresponding value of the conforming type.

declarations.name: ManagedAppConfigurationProvider
declarations.comment:
A class that provides configurations that an MDM admin provisions for a managed app or extension.

This class provides objects of a type you define, which decodes and validates the configuration that the framework receives from the MDM server.

The framework ingests the configuration in the form of a property list that the MDM server provides and passes to your type as a <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/swift/decoder>. Your type conforms to <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/swift/decodable> and parses the configuration according to your specification that the server admin conforms to when creating the property list.

If the decoder encounters a problem, it throws an error that the MDM admin can find in the device's event log.

declarations.name: ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider
declarations.comment:
A class that provides identities that an MDM admin provisions for a managed app or extension.

Create an instance of this class when your app needs to access identities that the MDM admin provisions for your app from their MDM server.

members.name: identifiers
members.signature: var identifiers: some AsyncSequence<Array<String>, Never> { get async }
members.comment:
An asynchronous sequence of arrays of identity identifiers provided by the MDM server.

Use ``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identity(withIdentifier:)`` to look up an identifier
to obtain the associated identity. The sequence yields an array of identifiers when:
* You begin iterating this property using `for await`.
* The list of identity identifiers changes.
* The value of one or more identities changes.

You define the values of the identifiers that an MDM admin can use. Define specific individual values or ranges of
values to group identities, or use the configuration to determine the meaning of the identifiers.

This property yields an empty array if the MDM admin hasn't provisioned any identities for your app.

members.name: identity
members.signature: func identity(withIdentifier identifier: String) async throws(ManagedAppError) -> SecIdentity
members.comment:
Provides an identity by its identifier.

The MDM server can update the identity at any time. After that, ``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers`` yields a new array of identifiers. Call this method again to obtain the updated identity.

The MDM server can change the available identities at any time. When that happens, the list of valid identifiers updates accordingly. For example, the list of valid identifiers might change between the time that the app accesses
``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers`` and then calls this method passing in one of its elements. So, the app needs to handle the case that this method throws ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier``.

When using identities in your app, observe the following caveats:

* Avoid putting identities in a file, database, or in the keychain. Storing an identity might not work as intended, for example, you're unable to retrieve a hardware-bound key after putting it in the keychain.
* <doc://com.apple.documentation/documentation/security/secidentity> references underlying keychain data that can disappear if the MDM admin removes the identity at runtime. Call this function as needed for a fresh reference rather than holding on to the result of a prior call for an extended period of time.
* For security reasons, avoid logging or displaying the identity's certificate or private key. Even though the certificate is a "public" certificate, it can contain sensitive information.

- Parameter identifier: The identifier of the requested identity. This function throws ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier`` if the value you supply isn't currently in ``ManagedAppIdentitiesProvider/identifiers``.
- Returns: The requested identity.
- Throws: ``ManagedAppError/invalidIdentifier`` if no identity exists with the specified identifier.
